mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a strengthening labor market, which typically boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE decreased by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% in a month signals a surge in consumer demand, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances where RSAFS increased by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% in a month signals an expansion in the supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as production capacity and corporate earnings grow.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings increase.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the months where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% each in a month signals a broad-based increase in demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity accelerates.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where both HOUST and RSAFS increased by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure in a high-interest-rate environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns diminish.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS was above 2% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.3% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a contraction in the supply side of the economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as production capacity and corporate earnings shrink.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO decreased by more than 0.5% in a month.
